item.title: The Shikoku 88-Temple Pilgrimage in Kochi — Guide
item.description: The Shikoku Pilgrimage is Japan’s most famous walking pilgrimage, a 1,200-kilometre circuit of 88 temples associated with the revered monk Kobo Daishi (Kukai), who was born on the island. Each of Shikoku’s four prefectures represents a stage of spiritual progress, and Kochi — old Tosa — is the longest and most demanding, known as the ‘dojo of ascetic training’. Its 16 temples are spread far apart along a wild stretch of Pacific coast and mountains, from Cape Muroto in the east to Cape Ashizuri in the far south, testing the pilgrim’s endurance and resolve.

item.title: Tochoji Temple and the Great Wooden Buddha — Guide
item.description: Tochoji is one of the oldest and most important temples in Fukuoka, founded by the great monk Kobo Daishi (Kukai) in the ninth century, making it central to Shingon Buddhism in the region. In the heart of Hakata, its grounds hold a striking vermilion five-storey pagoda and its greatest treasure: the Fukuoka Daibutsu, a magnificent seated wooden Buddha over 10 metres tall and one of the largest of its kind in Japan, carved from a single camphor tree.

item.title: Okunoin: Japan's Largest Cemetery Beneath the Cedars — Guide
item.description: Okunoin is the spiritual climax of Koyasan and the largest cemetery in Japan: a two-kilometre path winding beneath towering, centuries-old cedars past some 200,000 tombstones, memorials and mossy stupas, from feudal lords and famous samurai to company memorials and modern graves. At its far end stands the Gobyo, the mausoleum of Kobo Daishi, who is believed by the faithful not to have died but to rest in eternal meditation, awaiting the future Buddha — monks still carry him meals twice daily.
